QuestionStmt.S: A child stands on a weighing machine inside a lift. When the lift is going down with acceleration $g/3$, the machine shows a reading 20 N. When the lift goes upwards with acceleration $g/3$, the reading would be ($g =$ gravitational acceleration)

Solution.S:
When lift goes down with acceleration $a = g/3$:

Reading $R_1 = m(g - a) = m(g - g/3) = m(2g/3) = 20$ N.

When lift goes up with same acceleration:

Reading $R_2 = m(g + a) = m(g + g/3) = m(4g/3)$.

$$\frac{R_2}{R_1} = \frac{4g/3}{2g/3} = 2 \Rightarrow R_2 = 2 \times 20 = 40 \text{ N}$$

Thus the correct option is A: 40 N.
